Here is a translation and some interpretation of the Sumerian text you provided. Note that the text appears to be a literary or religious text with many divine names and ritual phrases. Some signs and passages are partially damaged or unclear (marked as X or […]), and some expressions are formulaic or idiomatic, so the translation is somewhat approximate:

---

1. ud re-a-ta ud an ki-bi-ta ba-an-[dim2-ma-ba]  
"Day of (the) foundation, day established in heaven and earth."

2. ĝi6 re-a-ta ĝi6 an ki-bi-ta /ba\-[an-dim2-ma-ba]  
"Brick of the foundation, brick established in heaven and earth."

3. [mu re]-a-/ta\ mu nam ba-[tar-ra-ba]  
"The name was formed as a fate (or destiny) of (the) month."

4. [da]-/nun\-na-ke4-ne ba-tu-ud-da-a-ba  
"(My) haven/place called Danunna was built."

5. dama-dinana nam-NIR.PA-še3 ba-tuku-a-ba  
"Dama-Dinana performed (or established) the honored name."

6. dama-dinana an ki-a ba-ḫal-ḫal-la-a-ba  
"Dama-Dinana thoroughly honored heaven and earth."

7. dama-dinana […] ba-a-peš u3-tud-da-a-ba  
"Dama-Dinana [...] made and established."

8. diĝir kurum6-ma-bi A X X unu2?-bi-še3 ba-ab-keše2-a-<ba>  
"The gods of the city — (unclear elements) — they did not neglect their annual duties."

9. diĝir šar2-šar2 kiĝ2-ĝa2 al-sug2-ge-eš diĝir tur-tur du2-lum im-il2-il2-e-ne  
"The great gods, mighty kings, exalted, the gods, restored the land, ruling with justice."

10. diĝir id2 <im> dun-dun-u3-ne saḫar-bi ḫa-ra-li im-dub-dub-be2-ne  
"The god Id (perhaps the river deity or landmark god), firmly established the temple, binding the boundary firmly."

11. diĝir im ar3-ar3-re-ne zi-bi inim am3-ma-ĝar-re-ne  
"The god of wind, causing storms, spoke words of life."

12. ud-ba ĝeštug2 daĝal mud diĝir šar2-šar2 ĝal2-ĝal2  
"On the day of the assembly, many gods, the great gods, were exalted."

13. den-ki-ke4 engur buru3 a-sur-ra ki diĝir na-me šag4-bi u6 nu-um-me  
"The divine lord Enki (Ea), lord of the subterranean freshwater, crowned with divine names, gave life without end."

14. ki-nu2-ni i3-nu2 u3 ku nu-um-zi-zi  
"His place, his dwelling and house were not empty."

15. diĝir er2-ra im-pad-pad-ne a-nir ĝal2 i3-ak im-me-ne  
"The god Erra was pacified, going forth mightily, he caused wrath to cease."

16. lu2 ku-ra i3-nu2-a-ra ki-nu2-bi nu-um-zi-zi-<ra>  
"The strong man, his dwelling-place, his place was not empty."

17. dnamma-ke4 ama palil u3-tud diĝir šar2-šar2-ra-ke4-ne  
"Namakke (the divine mother) honored and named the great gods."

18. er2-ra diĝir-re-e-ne dumu-ni-ir ba-ši-in-de6  
"Erra, the god, had a son born."

19. X mu-un-ši-nu2-u3-nam u3 mu-un-ši-ku-ku-na-nam  
"(Something) I will proclaim and I will establish."

20. [X] TE BA [… nu-mu-un]-zi-zi  
"(Something) word counts [...] I will not refuse."

21. dim3-me2-er šu dim2-dim2-ma-zu X gu2?-bi im-tu10-tu10-ne  
"As the honest one, he multiplied his hands, and (unclear) his cattle (? or temple vessels) abundantly."

---

**Summary and remarks:**  
This text contains ritualistic, religious, and mythological elements common in Sumerian temple hymns or incantations. It makes reference to divine foundations of heaven and earth, establishment of cities or temples (Danunna), the actions of various gods like Enki, Erra, and kinship relations, as well as ritual homage. Some parts are fragmentary or uncertain, so some lines include substitutes like "X" or bracketed phrases indicating reconstruction uncertainty.
